doc: Per-method classification used by the website to render Detailed Results chips, including historical published rows. Each method carries (a) a heaviness level anchored on the Python baseline wall time at the published bench scale (~2 MiB text input, 3 iters, 1 worker per cf6e8e7), and (b) an optional lifecycle status (active/deprecated/retired/retired-media) with the version it changed in. Match is case-insensitive substring on the bench label; longest match wins. Retired methods are absent from default artifacts and current benchmark runs; their old measurements remain here only to explain published historical results.

low.label: Low
low.explanation: Under 100 ms in Python at bench scale. Cheap and bounded. Safe to run on any host.

medium.label: Medium
medium.explanation: 100 ms to 1 s in Python at bench scale. Modest CPU + RAM. Fine on laptops.

high.label: High
high.explanation: 1 s to 5 s in Python at bench scale, or hundreds of MiB peak RSS. Use a dedicated build box if your laptop is small.

extreme.label: Extreme
extreme.explanation: Over 5 s in Python at bench scale, or multi-GiB peak RSS. Do not run on machines under 32 GiB RAM for production-scale inputs.

deprecated.label: Deprecated
deprecated.explanation: Public API stays callable so existing blobs / call sites keep working, but the method is no longer recommended for new code. Emits a deprecation warning at compile time and (where applicable) at first call. See CHANGELOG for the alternative.

retired.label: Retired
retired.explanation: Retired from default artifacts and current benchmark runs. Existing blobs still decode through an explicitly built compatibility artifact; historical result rows retain the retirement story.

retired-media.label: Retired 3.8.0 · compatibility build
retired-media.explanation: Retired, and excluded from default artifacts. Default C++, Java, and Python builds do not compile or package this method, its CLI command, its functional tests, or its benchmark. Existing data still decodes, but only from a compatibility artifact built with BASEFWX_ENABLE_RETIRED_MEDIA=1 at the same BaseFWX version; the switch cannot restore code that was never packaged.

methods.notes: SHA-512, fixed-size output. ~7 ms in Python at 2 MiB — near the OpenSSL throughput ceiling; C++/Java are within 30%.

Retired in 3.8.0 — non-standard chained hash (SHA-256 → SHA-1 → SHA-512 → SHA-256). Includes a SHA-1 compatibility hop and adds no sound security property. It is absent from default artifacts and current benchmarks; existing callers need a compatibility build. Use hash512 (SHA-512) or SHA3-512 for new code.
stdlib base64 — memory-bandwidth bound. ~21 ms in Python at 2 MiB.
Lightweight AEAD variant — Argon2id at reduced cost + AES-256-GCM. ~180 ms in Python at 2 MiB; the KDF dominates wall time.

Retired in 3.8.0 — SHA-256 with a custom prefilter and no added security. It is absent from default artifacts and current benchmarks; existing callers need a compatibility build. Use hash512 or SHA3-512 instead.

Encodes a file as a carrier PNG (audio source) or WAV (image source) — lossless container packing for steganographic transport. ~440 ms in Python at the historical 2 MiB run; C++ was ~17× faster because Python's Pillow PNG encoder has per-pixel dispatch overhead libpng doesn't. Output is structurally whole-buffer. Retired in 3.8.0 and dropped from default artifacts and current benchmarks; decoding existing files needs a compatibility build (BASEFWX_ENABLE_RETIRED_MEDIA=1).

Inverse of kFMe — decodes the carrier PNG/WAV back to original bytes. Retired in 3.8.0 and dropped from default artifacts and current benchmarks; decoding existing files needs a compatibility build (BASEFWX_ENABLE_RETIRED_MEDIA=1).

Streaming AEAD with chunked frames (1 MiB chunks) + optional ffmpeg pipe. ~470 ms in Python at 2 MiB. Note: Java is currently SLOWER than Python here because the small bench input doesn't amortize the per-frame AES-GCM Cipher init overhead; at 200 MiB Java overtakes by ~3×.

Legacy PNG-only carrier encoder (kFMe with the auto-detection removed). ~480 ms in Python in the historical run. Retired in 3.8.0 and dropped from default artifacts and current benchmarks; decoding existing files needs a compatibility build (BASEFWX_ENABLE_RETIRED_MEDIA=1).

Inverse of kFAe — decodes the legacy PNG carrier. Retired in 3.8.0 and dropped from default artifacts and current benchmarks; decoding existing files needs a compatibility build (BASEFWX_ENABLE_RETIRED_MEDIA=1).
Inverse of AN7. ~500 ms in Python at 2 MiB. Java is unexpectedly slower at this scale; see an7 note.

AN7 stealth anonymisation — chunked AES-CTR + sparse-flip + super-block permutation. ~520 ms in Python at 2 MiB. At this size Java is ~1.8× slower than Python because the per-chunk Cipher.init overhead doesn't amortize over only 2 chunks; the Java path is already optimized (cached ThreadLocal Cipher + Mac, in-place AES-CTR per commit 92a8a68). At ≥50 MiB inputs Java overtakes Python decisively.
Full AEAD — Argon2id at default cost + AES-256-GCM. ~710 ms in Python at 2 MiB; the KDF is ~90% of wall time and cannot be sped up without weakening security parameters.

Numeric encoding — turns arbitrary bytes into fixed-10-digit blocks with embedded FNV-1a checksum, for channels that only carry digits (SMS, phone fields, numeric-only DB columns). ~1.5 s in Python at 2 MiB. The bottleneck is the Python interpreter dispatch loop: ~524k iterations × ~4 arithmetic ops per iteration approaches the CPython speed ceiling for this algorithm. The arithmetic itself is on machine-sized integers (not bigints over the whole buffer), so NumPy can't help — uint64 overflows during the multiply step. The real fix is a C extension; PyPy already runs this ~30× faster than CPython by JIT-compiling the same loop. C++/Java are 18–30× faster than CPython for the same reason. Active because digit-only output has a legitimate purpose; the chip honestly reflects the interpreter gap.

🫡 b256 has been retired since BaseFWX 3.7.0. It was the first encoding method in BaseFWX, born in V1 back when this was a proof of concept and not yet a project. It served from day one; now it is absent from default artifacts and current benchmarks. Existing blobs still decode through a compatibility build. Use base64 / hash512 for new work. It's time to go. ❤️

Retired in 3.8.0 — reversible obfuscation with no security goal and an internal dependency on retired b256. It is absent from default artifacts and current benchmarks; existing callers need a compatibility build. Use standard base64 for transport or authenticated encryption for secrecy.

Password-required authenticated text payload. Version 3 uses AES-256-GCM with distinct HKDF/AAD domains and canonical standard base64. The password KDF dominates runtime; historical token expansion adds no cryptographic strength.

Password-or-master-keyed authenticated text payload. Version 3 uses AES-256-GCM with distinct HKDF/AAD domains and canonical standard base64. The password KDF dominates runtime; historical token expansion adds no cryptographic strength.

Media cipher — AEAD over a whole pixel/sample buffer, with an optional archive trailer that stores the encrypted original for exact restore. Retired in 3.8.0 and dropped from default artifacts and current benchmarks; decoding existing files needs a compatibility build (BASEFWX_ENABLE_RETIRED_MEDIA=1).
File-mode wrapper around b512 — KDF + AEAD over the whole file. ~7.3 s in Python at the bench input; multi-GiB files extend linearly.
File-mode wrapper around pb512. ~8.6 s in Python at the bench input; multi-GiB files extend linearly.
